submitted.rationale: Index 30 (Ni0.17Sb0.83) had the highest measured EQE, 1.08%. That is about 23x index 27 (0.047%) and about 70x index 21, the NiSb2O6 composition (0.015%). EQE rises sharply at the Sb-rich edge.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 0.015%. MACE puts stoichiometric trirutile NiSb2O6 on the hull, but it performed poorly.
Measured EQE 0.047%, so there is no maximum between 21 and 30.
Not measured. This is the Ni-rich end, which is mostly NiO: p-type with an experimental gap of about 3.7 eV, above the 3.2 eV illumination, so it is unlikely to work as a photoanode.

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts trirutile NiSb2O6 on the hull (0 eV/atom), so index 21 (Sb 0.66) should be a single stable phase. The MEGNet HSE gap of 0.04 eV is uninformative because it is likely an artifact for open-shell Ni2+. The 3.2 eV photons are well above the realistic gap.

Against the Ni-rich middle: MACE puts Ni2Sb2O7 at 0.27 eV/atom above the hull, so compositions near Sb 0.5 are probably phase mixtures. The other Sb-rich ternary (Sb 0.667) has an HSE gap of about 3.6 eV. Index 21 gave a low EQE (0.015%), so I'm testing the Sb-rich end (index 30), which should be NiSb2O6 plus Sb oxide.

Mostly uninformative and mildly against the Ni-rich end. MEGNet gives NiO an HSE gap of 2.4 eV, but the experimental gap is about 3.7 eV, which is above the 3.2 eV photons. NiO is also p-type, so it is a poor photoanode. The measured data show EQE rising steeply toward the Sb-rich end, so I'm spending the last measurement on index 27 in case the maximum is inside the range and not at the edge.
